entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11654"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 33</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ezek.33.1-Ezek.33.33">Eze 33:1-33</reference>. Renewal of Ezekiel's Commission, Now that He Is Again to Address His Countrymen, and in a New Tone.</title> <div sID="gen21107" type="x-p"/> Heretofore his functions had been chiefly threatening; from this point, after the evil had got to its worst in the overthrow of Jerusalem, the consolatory element preponderates.<div eID="gen21107" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21108" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11654"/><hi type="bold">2. to the children of thy people--</hi>whom he had been forbidden to address from <reference osisRef="Ezek.24.26">Eze 24:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.24.27">27</reference>, till Jerusalem was overthrown, and the "escaped" came with tidings of the judgment being completed. So now, in <reference osisRef="Ezek.33.21">Eze 33:21</reference>, the tidings of the fact having arrived, he opens his heretofore closed lips to the Jews. In the interval he had prophesied as to foreign nations. The former part of the chapter, at <reference osisRef="Ezek.33.2-Ezek.33.20">Eze 33:2-20</reference>, seems to have been imparted to Ezekiel on the evening previous (<reference osisRef="Ezek.33.22">Eze 33:22</reference>), being a preparation for the latter part (<reference osisRef="Ezek.33.23-Ezek.33.33">Eze 33:23-33</reference>) imparted after the tidings had come. This accounts for the first part standing without intimation of the date, which was properly reserved for the latter part, to which the former was the anticipatory introduction [Fairbairn].<div eID="gen21108" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21109" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">watchman--</hi><reference osisRef="Ezek.33.1-Ezek.33.9">Eze 33:1-9</reference> exhibit Ezekiel's office as a spiritual watchman; so in <reference osisRef="Ezek.3.16-Ezek.3.21">Eze 3:16-21</reference>; only here the duties of the earthly watchman (compare <reference osisRef="2Sam.18.24">2Sa 18:24</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Sam.18.25">25</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.9.17">2Ki 9:17</reference>) are detailed first, and then the application is made to the spiritual watchman's duty (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.21.6-Isa.21.10">Is 21:6-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.9.8">Ho 9:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hab.2.1">Ha 2:1</reference>). "A man of their coasts" is a man specially chosen for the office out of their whole number. So <reference osisRef="Judg.18.2">Jud 18:2</reference>, "five men from their coasts"; also the Hebrew of <reference osisRef="Gen.47.2">Ge 47:2</reference>; implying the care needed in the choice of the watchman, the spiritual as well as the temporal (<reference osisRef="Acts.1.21">Ac 1:21</reference>, 22, 24-26; <reference osisRef="1Tim.5.22">1Ti 5:22</reference>). <div eID="gen21109" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 33 Eze 33:1-33 . Renewal of Ezekiel's Commission, Now that He Is Again to Address His Countrymen, and in a New Tone. Heretofore his functions had been chiefly threatening; from this point, after the evil had got to its worst in the overthrow of Jerusalem, the consolatory element preponderates. 2. to the children of thy people-- whom he had been forbidden to address from Eze 24:26 , 27 , till Jerusalem was overthrown, and the "escaped" came with tidings of the judgment being completed. So now, in Eze 33:21 , the tidings of the fact having arrived, he opens his heretofore closed lips to the Jews. In the interval he had prophesied as to foreign nations. The former part of the chapter, at Eze 33:2-20 , seems to have been imparted to Ezekiel on the evening previous ( Eze 33:22 ), being a preparation for the latter part ( Eze 33:23-33 ) imparted after the tidings had come. This accounts for the first part standing without intimation of the date, which was properly reserved for the latter part, to which the former was the anticipatory introduction [Fairbairn]. watchman-- Eze 33:1-9 exhibit Ezekiel's office as a spiritual watchman; so in Eze 3:16-21 ; only here the duties of the earthly watchman (compare 2Sa 18:24 , 25 ; 2Ki 9:17 ) are detailed first, and then the application is made to the spiritual watchman's duty (compare Is 21:6-10 ; Ho 9:8 ; Ha 2:1 ). "A man of their coasts" is a man specially chosen for the office out of their whole number. So Jud 18:2 , "five men from their coasts"; also the Hebrew of Ge 47:2 ; implying the care needed in the choice of the watchman, the spiritual as well as the temporal ( Ac 1:21 , 22, 24-26; 1Ti 5:22 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11662"/><div sID="gen21119" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11662"/>11. To meet the Jews' cry of despair in <reference osisRef="Ezek.33.10">Eze 33:10</reference>, Ezekiel here cheers them by the assurance that God has no pleasure in their death, but that they should repent and live (<reference osisRef="2Pet.3.9">2Pe 3:9</reference>). A yearning tenderness manifests itself here, notwithstanding all their past sins; yet with it a holiness that abates nothing of its demands for the honor of God's authority. God's righteousness is vindicated as in <reference osisRef="Ezek.3.18-Ezek.3.21">Eze 3:18-21</reference> and <reference osisRef="Ezek.18.1-Ezek.18.32">Eze 18:1-32</reference>, by the statement that each should be treated with the closest adaptation of God's justice to his particular case. <div eID="gen21119" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11666"/><div sID="gen21124" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11666"/><hi type="bold">21. twelfth year ... tenth month--</hi>a year and a half after the capture of the city (<reference osisRef="Jer.39.2">Jr 39:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.52.5">52:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.52.6">6</reference>), in the eleventh year and fourth month. The one who escaped (as foretold, <reference osisRef="Ezek.24.26">Eze 24:26</reference>) may have been so long on the road through fear of entering the enemy's country [Henderson]; or, the singular is used for the plural in a collective sense, "the escaped remnant." Compare similar phrases, "the escaped of Moab," <reference osisRef="Isa.15.9">Is 15:9</reference>; "He that escapeth of them," <reference osisRef="Amos.9.1">Am 9:1</reference>. Naturally the reopening of the prophet's mouth for consolation would be deferred till the number of the escaped remnant was complete: the removal of such a large number would easily have occupied seventeen or eighteen months. <div eID="gen21124" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11671"/><div sID="gen21133" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11671"/><hi type="bold">27. shall fall by the sword--</hi>The very object of their confidence would be the instrument of their destruction. Thinking to "stand" by it, by it they shall "fall." Just retribution! Some fell by the sword of Ishmael; others by the Chaldeans in revenge for the murder of Gedaliah (Jr 40:1-44:30).<div eID="gen21133" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21134" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">caves--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Judg.6.2">Jud 6:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.13.6">1Sa 13:6</reference>). In the hilly parts of Judea there were caves almost inaccessible, as having only crooked and extremely narrow paths of ascent, with rock in front stretching down into the valleys beneath perpendicularly [Josephus, Wars of the Jews, 1.16.4]. <div eID="gen21134" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 27. shall fall by the sword-- The very object of their confidence would be the instrument of their destruction. Thinking to "stand" by it, by it they shall "fall."
